NPTEL Online Certification Course
             Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee
Course Name: Introduction to Application of Artificial Intelligence to Robotics
                             Instructor: Prof. Pushparaj Mani Pathak

                 WEEK 10: ASSIGNMENT 10


   Q.1  A robot preprocesses the word “running” using two different methods:
        Method A → runn
        Method B → run
        Which statement is correct?

         (A) Method A is lemmatization, while Method B is stemming

          (B) Method A is stemming, while Method B is lemmatization

          (C) Both methods are stemming because both shorten the word

         (D) Both methods are lemmatization because both produce a base form

          Explanation: Stemming removes word endings mechanically and may produce a non-
        word such as “runn”. Lemmatization produces the meaningful base form “run”.
          Refer slide 9 of Lecture 46: Natural Language Processing


   Q.2   The vocabulary is unordered as: [chair, pick, red, ball, near]. What is the one-hot
           vector for near?

         (A) [0,0,1,0,0]

          (B) [0,1,0,0,0]

          (C) [0,0,0,1,0]

         (D) [1,0,0,0,0]

          Explanation: Vocabulary in alphabetically ordered as: [ball, chair, near, pick, red]
          “near” occupies the third position in the five-word vocabulary, so its corresponding
           position is 1 and all others are 0.
          Refer slide 14 of Lecture 46: Natural Language Processing

   Q.3   Consider a single attention head with query  𝑞𝑖 = [2, 1],  keys 𝑘1 = [3, 1], 𝑘2 =
            [1,2], 𝑘3 = [0,1] and key vector  size 𝑑𝑘= 2. Which option gives the  correct
          normalized attention scores approximately?

         (A) [0.88, 0.11, 0.013]

          (B) [0.50, 0.30, 0.20]

          (C) [0.67, 0.24, 0.09]

         (D) [0.86, 0.10, 0.04]





                                                                                   1 | P a g e

Q.4  A transformer receives a sequence containing 12 tokens. Each token is represented by
      an embedding vector containing 64 features. The model uses a single attention head
       with separate projection matrices for Query, Key, and Value:
                      𝑊𝑄, 𝑊𝐾∈ℝ64×16, 𝑊𝑉∈ℝ64×20

      Which option correctly gives the dimensions of 𝑋, 𝑄, 𝐾 and 𝑉?

      (A) 𝑋: 12 × 64, 𝑄: 12 × 16, 𝐾: 12 × 16, 𝑉: 12 × 20

      (B) 𝑋: 64 × 12, 𝑄: 16 × 12, 𝐾: 16 × 12, 𝑉: 20 × 12

      (C) 𝑋: 12 × 64, 𝑄: 12 × 64, 𝐾: 12 × 64, 𝑉: 12 × 64

      (D) 𝑋: 64 × 12, 𝑄: 64 × 16, 𝐾: 64 × 16, 𝑉: 64 × 20





                                                                               2 | P a g e

slides.title: Explanation: Since there are 12 tokens and each token has 64 features, the input matrix
slides.text:
Explanation: Since there are 12 tokens and each token has 64 features, the input matrix
         is
                              𝑋∈ℝ12×64
      Then,
             𝑄= 𝑋𝑊𝑄: (12 × 64)(64 × 16) = 12 × 16
             𝐾= 𝑋𝑊𝐾: (12 × 64)(64 × 16) = 12 × 16
      and
             𝑉= 𝑋𝑊𝑉: (12 × 64)(64 × 16) = 12 × 20.
       Therefore,

                      𝑋: 12 × 64, 𝑄: 12 × 16, 𝐾: 12 × 16, 𝑉: 12 × 20
      Refer slides 9-19 of Lecture 47: Transformers


Q.5  A 1-D CNN processes a sequence of 100 acoustic frames. If its kernel of width 2
      moves by two frames at each step, what is the output sequence length? (ignore
       padding)

      (A) 50

      (B) 99

      (C)100

      (D) 1

       Explanation: If the kernel moves one frame at a time (stride=1), the output sequence
                                                                                     100
         is the same length as the input sequence. If the stride=2 then output sequence is  =
                                                                                      2
      50. (kernel centers are at 1, 3, 5, … , 99, so total are 50)
      Refer slide 18 of Lecture 48: AI based Speech Recognition


Q.6   Suppose a decoder generates three tokens with conditional probabilities:
                                   𝑃(𝑦1|𝑋) = 0.5
                                     𝑃(𝑦2|𝑦1, 𝑋) = 0.4
                                   𝑃(𝑦3|𝑦1, 𝑦2, 𝑋) = 0.2
     What is the probability assigned to the complete three-token sequence?

      (A) 0.1

      (B) 0.11

      (C) 0.04

      (D) 1.1





                                                                               3 | P a g e

Q.7   Consider the following interaction:
       User: “I enjoy playing the piano.”
      Robot: “Is the piano your favorite instrument?”
      Match the AIML tags in Column I with the corresponding example/function in
     Column II.

      Column I — AIML Tag  Column II — Example related to the interaction

        P. <category>              1. "Is the piano your favorite instrument?"

       Q. <pattern>                2. Hiddenly stores "your piano" as the conversational
                                  context

       R. <template>              3. Complete conversational rule containing the trigger
                              and response

        S. <set_it>                  4. "I ENJOY PLAYING *"

     Which of the following gives the correct matching?

      (A) P–3, Q–4, R–1, S–2

      (B) P–3, Q–1, R–4, S–2

      (C) P–2, Q–4, R–1, S–3

      (D) P–4, Q–3, R–1, S–2

       Explanation:
      <category> → complete conversational knowledge unit
       <pattern> → trigger/input pattern
      <template> → programmed response
       <set_it> → stores the processed value in conversational context
      The structure follows the AIML pattern-matching and context-memory example.
      Refer slide 14 of Lecture 49: Conversational AI & Human-Robot Interaction


Q.8  A robot uses the traditional pipeline:
      Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) →Large Language Model (LLM) → Text-to-
      Speech (TTS)
         If the ASR incorrectly transcribes “turn right” as “turn light,” which downstream
      consequence is most consistent?

      (A) The LLM is guaranteed to recover the original audio signal.

      (B) The transcription error can propagate into the LLM and affect the generated
       response/action.

                                                                               4 | P a g e

slides.title: (C) TTS automatically corrects the semantic error.
slides.text:
(C) TTS automatically corrects the semantic error.

      (D) The error disappears because ASR and LLM are independent.

       Explanation: Cumulative error as a major limitation: transcription errors from ASR
      can cascade into the LLM.
      Refer slide 17 of Lecture 49: Conversational AI & Human-Robot Interaction


Q.9  A student freezes the pretrained CNN and trains only a new classifier on top of its
        features. Which strategy has been implemented?

      (A) Full fine-tuning

      (B) Partial fine-tuning

      (C) Feature extraction

      (D) Multimodal fusion

       Explanation: Feature extraction trains only the classifier while retaining the pretrained
       feature extractor.
      Refer slide 15 of Lecture 50: Developing An Emotion Engine For Robots


Q.10  Two users say exactly the same sentence: “I finished the assignment.”
      User A previously told the robot they were struggling with the assignment. User B
       previously said they found it very easy.
      According  to  the memory-based  dialogue  architecture, why  could  the  robot
       appropriately respond differently?

      (A) The memory-augmented context differs between users, even though the immediate
       input sentence is the same

      (B) ASR produces different words for the two users

      (C) TTS automatically changes the semantic meaning

      (D) The robot's emotion state is independent of conversation context

       Explanation: The stored context and estimated emotions are jointly used to plan an
       appropriate response.
      Refer slide 23 of Lecture 50: Developing An Emotion Engine For Robots
